sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 25.06.2020.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 25.06.2020 at about 14.30 hours, the petitioner parked his Mahendra Bolero pickup vehicle bearing No. KA-04-C-7839 on the left side of the road on NH.44, near Gurukula Hostel, Chitteboinpally village, Jadcheri Taluk, Telangana and for taking water bottle when he open the door of the said vehicle, at that time the driver of Maruthi Dezire car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128 came from back side and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to SVC Medical College and Hospital,
Yenugonda, Mahabubangar, Telengana, wherein first aid was done and later he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent huge amount towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines,
conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

entities.text:
SVC Medical College and Hospital,
Yenugonda
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Prior to the accident,
petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as owner cum driver of Bolero goods vehicle and furniture exhibition organiser and earning Rs.70,000/- to Rs.80,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.2 remained absent hence, placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.

Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the Swift Dzire car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128 and the liability of this respondent, if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, the accident was happened due to negligence on the part of petitioner himself and there is no negligence on the part of driver of the car.
Also contended that the driver of the car was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.

The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly Surendra Kumar vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91855541/
2 excessive and exorbitant.

sentences.text: Hence, the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 25.6.2020 at about 2.30 p.m. on NH-44,
near Gurukul Hostel, Chitteboinpally, Jadcherla, Mehaboobnagara District,
Telengala State, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Swift Dezire car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128 in an actionable negligence?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, at what rate?
From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 19.
Dr. Avinash Parthasarathy, Professor of Orthopaedics at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital is examined as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P20 to 23.
In spite of sufficient opportunities, the respondents did not chose to adduce evidence.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, accident report form and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 5.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Sandu Sukpal Singh who is also eye witness to the alleged accident.
The Ex.P1 & 2 is in consonance with the contents of petition.
In the Ex.P1 & 2 the informant alleged the rash and negligent driving by the driver of car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128.

sentences.text: After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar and sketch was conducted.
On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar and the rough sketch therein, the alleged accident place is in the left side of the road.

The mahazar also discloses that the car bearing No.
TS-07-UE-6128 has dashed against the door of the bolero pick up vehicle bearing No. KA-04-C- 7839.
The Ex.P4 is IMV report wherein the car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128 has got damaged in its front portion and also the radiator of the said car is also got damaged.
This establishes the severity of the accident and also negligence on the part of driver of car bearing No. TS-07- UE-6128.
The Ex.P15 photographs of the accident also establishes the negligence on the part of driver of car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128.

As per the photographs marked at Ex.P15, the bolero pick up bearing No. KA-04- C-7839 was parked on the mud road and the driver of car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128 dahsed the said bolero pick up which is parked on the mud road.

Thus, the contents of Ex.P3 mahazar and rough sketch along with photographs marked at Ex.P15 supported the case of the petitioner regarding the rash and negligence driving by the driver of the car bearing No.
TS-07-UE-6128.
11.

Ex.P5 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the offending car bearing No.
TS-07-UE- 6128 wherein, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128.

It is very important to note that the driver of car bearing No.
TS-07-UE-6128 dashed against the bolero pick up which was parked on the mud road.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner.
12. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But both the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of offending car bearing No. TS- 07-UE-6128.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Swift Dezire Car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128 13.
The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence driving.

The respondent no.2 even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of driver of bolero pick up vehicle i.e.,
petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
The respondent No.1 & 2 even after sufficient opportunity have not lead any evidence to disprove the contents of these documents.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the driver of the offending car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128 for the offences punishable under Sec. 338 of IPC.

Hence, by relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 5, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128.
15.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

16. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 25.09.2022 which is caused by the driver of the Swift Dezire Car bearing No. TS-07- UE-6128 which belonging to respondent No.2.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
17.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.2.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY :-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 45 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P12 also shows that the petitioner was aged about 45 years at the time of accident.
In the petition itself he has averred that he was admitted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital on 26.06.2020 and discharged on 07.07.2020 and again admitted on 12.8.2021 and discharged on 24.8.2021.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P10 the petitioner sustained left humerus shaft fracture with radial nerve neuropraxia, left isolated ulna fracture and left both bone leg fracture.
He underwent procedure of CRIF with IMIL Nail for tibia and ORIF with plate and screw for humerus and ulna.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.30,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

sentences.text: 5 b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P17, amounting to Rs.1,18,304/-.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.1,18,400/-.

c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that he was working as owner cum driver of bolero goods vehicle and furniture exhibition organiser and earning Rs.70,000/- to 80,000/- p.m.

To prove the said fact the petitioner has produced bank statement as per Ex.P14 and also letter at Ex.P13 issued by one Ahmed furniture wherein they have stated that the petitioner was earning Rs.75,000/- to Rs.80,000/- p.m. on commission basis.
On perusal of Ex.P14 there is no evidence is available to hold that per month Rs.75,000/- to Rs.80,000/- was earning by the petitioner.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.14,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2020.
As per the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P10- the petitioner was admitted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital for 25 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total three months period including 25 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,500 X 3 months = Rs.43,500/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr. Avinash Parthasarathy, Orthopedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital as PW.2, through him case sheets,
recent clinical notes, disability assessment report and X-rays are marked at Ex.P.20 to 23.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained left both bone leg fracture, left humeral shaft fracture with radial nerve plasty and left ulna fracture.
He underwent OR & IF with plate and screws for left humerus and ulna fracture and CR & IF with IM Nail for left tibia fracture.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered physical impairment in left upper limb at 70% and whole body disability at 24%.
The PW.2 doctor also deposed that the implants are not yet removed.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross- examination.
Further PW.2 has also stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which may costs Rs.40,000/-.
According to the petitioner he was working as owner cum driver of bolero goods vehicle and furniture exhibition organiser.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 insurance company vehemently argued that the petitioner has not produced the account details after the date of accident as such, as the petitioner still earning the same, submitted that he has not sustained any financial disability.
But the implants are still present in the hand and legs of the petitioner.
Certainly the said injury will not allow the petitioner to work like earlier.
He need some assistance or support for this work.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 15% to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced his Aadhar card marked at Ex.P12, as per this document the year of birth of the petitioner is shown as 1975.
The accident was occurred in the year-2020.

So, as on the Surendra Kumar vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91855541/
6 date of the accident the petitioner was aged 45 years.

sentences.text: As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '14'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.14,500/- X 12 X 14 X 15% =Rs.3,65,400/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ;
As per Ex.P10 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 25 days.
By considering the nature of injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 25 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.25,000/- in total.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
h)Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.40,000/-.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.20,000/- under this head.
i) The petitioner also produced transportation bills as per Ex.P16.
Out of the bill marked at Sl. No.102 is pertaining to the ambulance bill of date of accident and the other bills are pertaining to the traveling of the petitioner for follow up treatment.
Admittedly the implants are still present and the petitioner need some traveling assistance for his follow up treatment as such, he is entitled for the reimbursement of the bills marked at Ex.P16.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of Rs.29,700/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 30,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 1,18,400/-
c) Towards loss of income Rs. 43,500/-

18.
Liability:- According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the car bearing No. TS-07-UE-6128 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.1 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.2.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
19.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.6,67,000/- (Rupees Six lakhs sixty seven thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,500 X 3 months = Rs.43,500/- during the laid up period.
